findings.baseline: The report recipes explain selected-version arrows and configuration ownership but do not spell out successful reports containing unresolved nodes.
findings.evidence: Gradle v8.14.3 upstream report and insight integration tests expect FAILED nodes in reports. An installed9.6.1 isolated fixture returned exit0/BUILD SUCCESSFUL from both diagnostic tasks despite a missing org.example:codec:1.0 module.
findings.consequence: An agent could accept command success as successful dependency resolution or interpret an arrow to a missing component as a verified selection.
findings.correction: Read exit status and unresolved diagnostics together; preserve error details and inspect affected coordinate/repository/constraint/variant; no success claim from the report alone.
findings.validation: Missing-module negative fixture: report exit0 with FAILED and consuming task exit1. Raw output preserved.

findings.baseline: The package separates graph from deployed contents but leaves the earlier boundary between metadata graph and acquired dependency files implicit.
findings.evidence: Pinned8.14.3 graph/artifact resolution model; installed9.6.1 POM-only fixture has an apparently resolved graph with no FAILED nodes, then strict runtime-file consumption cannot obtain codec-1.0.jar.
findings.consequence: A graph-only rerun could be reported as a completed artifact-resolution repair, or a valid version selection could be changed when the missing artifact is the actual defect.
findings.correction: Distinguish graph from file acquisition; preserve correct graph findings and rerun the actual affected consumer task rather than speculative version changes.
findings.validation: POM-only: reports0 without FAILED, consumer1. Same POM plus valid local JAR: reports0 and consumer0; copied bytes match source SHA256.
